newsitem.title: USA: Calif court says LA yield burning case to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Calif court says LA yield burning case to proceed.

text.p: The California Supreme Court rejected a petition by Lazard Freres & Co to dismiss Los Angeles County's "yield burning" case against the firm, ending a year of Lazard maneuvers to head off the $14 million challenge, the court said.

John Phillips, a partner with Phillips & Cohen, which is representing the county, told Reuters on Thursday that Lazard's motion had been the third and last opportunity for the Wall Street firm to win dismissal of the case, Los Angeles Metropolitan Transit Authority v Lazard Freres & Co.
The decision opens the way for the San Francisco County Superior Court to begin discovery proceedings in the case, Phillips said.

The case is the first legal challenge nationwide by a municipality to yield burning, which refers to allegations that bond undewriters overcharge states and localities for U.S. Treasury securities they bought to help them refinance their oustanding bonds.
The county's lawsuit charges that Lazard, which was financial adviser on authority refinancings from 1990 to 1995, illegally overpriced the Treasuries bought by the authority.
"They lost this motion in the superior, the appellate and now the supreme court, which is the last appellate court they can go through," Phillips said.
"This has been a stalling tactic by Lazard to delay the inevitable. Now discovery will commence so that we will get access to all of their documents and records" about the deals, Phillips added.
A response from Lazard officials was not yet available.
The lawsuit was first filed by former municipal finance banker Michael Lissack under California's false claims statute. The Los Angeles County authority joined the lawsuit eight months later.
